summary: Oral SCC rules for surface epithelium, invasive nests/cords, keratinization, dispersed invasive front, perineural/vascular interfaces, and heterogeneous supporting tissues.

rules.claim: Do not partially transect or relabel surface squamous epithelium during a generic invasive tumor burden edit.
rules.required_observation: Trace the epithelial surface, rete architecture, basement-membrane interface, dysplastic/in-situ area, and any true invasive breach on H&E.
exceptions: A dedicated dysplasia-to-invasion or ulceration primitive with a separate contract.
counterexamples: Growing an invasive nest upward through intact remote mucosa.
Deleting a strip of surface epithelium to smooth the tumor boundary.
expected_morphology: Unrequested surface epithelium remains continuous and anatomically attached.
forbidden_morphology: Artificial epithelial gap, half-thickness cut, detached remnant, or false invasion breach.
known_limitations: ORCA does not label normal/dysplastic surface epithelium separately from Other tissue.

rules.claim: Avoid partial internal cuts, deep slots, narrow necks, or remote islands that make a cohesive invasive nest or cord anatomically implausible.
rules.required_observation: Trace the entire local nest/cord boundary and compare epithelial cohesion and stromal reaction along the proposed anchor.
exceptions: Discohesive or satellite invasion must be explicitly identified and use its own rule.
counterexamples: A deep wedge cut from a short edge of a large cohesive nest.
An expansion creating a detached square tumor island.
expected_morphology: A shallow distributed boundary displacement continuous with the same nest or cord.
forbidden_morphology: V-shaped notch, long narrow tunnel, abrupt angular edge, detached island, or unexplained bridge.
known_limitations: Numeric curvature/depth calibration needs oral-site and scale stratification.

rules.claim: Preserve the concentric relationship between viable squamous tumor and central keratin; do not fill keratinized centers with tumor or seed growth from detached keratin debris.
rules.required_observation: Identify the complete keratin pearl, viable peripheral tumor rim, detached surface keratin/debris, and any necrosis.
exceptions: A dedicated differentiation/keratinization primitive with separate semantic support.
counterexamples: Morphological closing that fills a keratin pearl center.
Creating a tumor island around free keratin debris in Other tissue.
expected_morphology: Peripheral viable nest and central keratin remain topologically coherent.
forbidden_morphology: Center filling, pearl bisection, keratin-debris seeding, or false new pearl.
known_limitations: ORCA carcinoma masks do not separately label viable tumor, keratin, and necrosis.

rules.claim: Small satellites, cords, and single-cell invasion at an aggressive front must not be connected into a solid mass or treated as annotation noise.
rules.required_observation: Inspect cluster size, cell cohesion, distance from the main tumor, stromal response, and whether each focus is true carcinoma rather than inflammation/artifact.
exceptions: A coarse profile may outline aggregate carcinoma, but must still preserve visible non-tumor gaps and protected background.
counterexamples: Taking a convex hull around separate satellite nests.
Removing a tiny true tumor nest because it is below a component-size threshold.
expected_morphology: Satellite/discohesive foci retain their spacing and are edited only from verified same-component tissue interfaces.
forbidden_morphology: Broad bridge, forced solidification, satellite deletion, or remote tumor creation.
known_limitations: Worst-pattern-of-invasion assessment may require a wider field than a patch.

rules.claim: Do not create, erase, or bridge perineural or lymphovascular invasion during a generic burden edit.
rules.required_observation: Identify nerve fascicle/perineurium or endothelial-lined vascular space and inspect the tumor relationship around or within it.
exceptions: A dedicated perineural/lymphovascular invasion primitive with containment and continuity constraints.
counterexamples: Growing tumor through a nerve to connect two nests.
Filling a vessel lumen with tumor during smoothing.
Erasing a small invaded nerve because it is labeled Other tissue.
expected_morphology: Nerve/vessel geometry and its pre-edit relationship to tumor remain unchanged.
forbidden_morphology: False encirclement, lumen filling, wall crossing, nerve bisection, or removal of an existing relationship.
known_limitations: Definitive small-vessel or nerve identification can require ancillary stains or larger context.

rules.claim: Use stroma-specific reasoning only where H&E supports stromal tissue; do not treat muscle, salivary tissue, mucosa, inflammation, keratin, vessel, nerve, or ORCA Other tissue as interchangeable stroma.
rules.required_observation: Identify the histologic substrate in H&E and intersect its allowable use with the annotation profile's actual ontology.
exceptions: A coarse profile may support generic non-carcinoma-to-carcinoma editing but cannot claim a stroma-specific change.
counterexamples: Calling all ORCA gray pixels stroma.
Growing tumor through skeletal muscle with a stroma dilation template.
Using salivary ducts as Other-tissue fill.
expected_morphology: The selected boundary is H&E-compatible with the primitive and respects protected structures.
forbidden_morphology: Cross-muscle bulk fill, salivary-unit transection, immune/keratin seeding, or unsupported stroma statements.
known_limitations: ORCA has no tissue subtype label inside non-carcinoma tissue.

rules.claim: Prefer a broad verified carcinoma/non-carcinoma tissue interface matching the same tumor architecture; spread area along the front before increasing depth.
rules.required_observation: Compare interface length, target area, maximum depth, tumor cohesion/keratinization, and adjacent H&E tissue.
exceptions: If no compatible interface can satisfy the area budget, abstain rather than use background or an unrelated tissue boundary.
counterexamples: Meeting a large area target by one narrow inward notch.
Selecting a black/gray ORCA background edge as the invasive front.
expected_morphology: Shallow, distributed, H&E-supported deformation of one existing invasive front.
forbidden_morphology: Deep slot, geometric wedge, background crossing, architecture mismatch, or remote island.
known_limitations: Quantitative thresholds require oral-site, scale, and annotation-profile calibration.
